A club FAQ with RAG, citations, and a small eval set
A giant net trained from scratch with no labeled data
Demo screenshots only, with metrics postponed until later
15.explanation: Finishable scope plus evidence beats theater.

15.prompt: What must a capstone README include?
choices: Only screenshots and a catchy project title, even thoug
How to run, what data, metrics, and known limitations
Production secrets pasted in plaintext for graders
A promise that the system has no limitations section
15.explanation: Runnable and honest documentation is part of the grade.

15.prompt: Teammate wants multimodal agents, fine-tuning, and a mobile app in two weeks. Best move?
choices: Keep the full scope and sleep less until everything ships
Cut to one vertical slice with eval cases and risk notes
Skip evaluation so there is more time for animations
Start three repos so each person can invent a different product
15.explanation: Depth on a thin slice is the advanced studio move.

15.prompt: When should the evaluation set be authored?
choices: After the UI polish is finished and screenshots look great
Before polish, so success criteria drive the build
Never, if the demo path works once on a laptop
Only if a teacher explicitly grades the CSV file

15.prompt: What belongs in a capstone risk register?
choices: Only the names of libraries used in package.json
Failure modes, privacy notes, oversight
A statement that risks disappear after the demo day
GPU benchmarks with no link to user harm

15.prompt: Which artifact best supports a “ready to demo” claim?
choices: A single polished screenshot with no failure cases
Metrics on representative cases plus recovery paths
A promise that the model is smart enough in general
A hidden prompt nobody else can inspect
15.explanation: Readiness needs reproducible evidence and known limits.

15.prompt: Why run a focused red-team session before studio day?
choices: Red teams are only for companies with security staff
Abuse and hard cases reveal gaps while you can still fix them
Red-teaming replaces the need for any metric table while skippi
It guarantees the system will pass every future audit
15.explanation: Find failures before the defense, not during it.

16.prompt: What makes a capstone audit credible on defense day?
choices: Saying “trust us” because the happy-path demo looked smooth
Evidence, mitigations, residual risk, and a monitoring plan
Hiding failures so judges never see an imperfect slice
Reporting only marketing metrics with no limitations

16.prompt: Best order for a defense script?
choices: Show failures first with no problem statement or metrics
Claim → evidence → hard failure → mitigation → residual risk
Only show the UI theme and skip evaluation tables, which often
Promise perfection, then refuse questions about limits
16.explanation: Engineers earn trust by structuring claims and limits.

16.prompt: Which student claim matches this track’s graduation standard?
choices: I only know prompts; metrics and fairness are optional
I can build and evaluate AI systems with documented risks
Models are always fair once accuracy crosses ninety percent
Deploying without logs is fine if the demo impressed people
16.explanation: Creator plus auditor mindset is the goal.

16.prompt: Why demo a hard failure on purpose?
choices: To sabotage the project grade with avoidable mistakes while
To show recovery design and honest understanding of limits
Because judges forbid happy-path demonstrations entirely
To prove evaluation metrics are never worth collecting
16.explanation: Showing failures with mitigations is maturity.

choices: Risk that disappears the moment a mitigation is written down
Risk that remains after controls, and must still be owned
Only the risk of the GPU overheating in the classroom
A synonym for training loss on the final epoch
16.explanation: Mitigation reduces risk; it rarely deletes it.

choices: So graders can verify claims beyond a one-time performance
So the team never needs a README or metric table
So failures can be edited out of every recorded run
So model weights can stay secret from the builders themselves
16.explanation: Reproducibility turns a show into evidence.

16.prompt: Which closing recommendation is most advanced?
choices: Ship everywhere immediately with no monitoring owner
Recommend a bounded release, named owners
Claim the system has no limits worth mentioning
Delete the audit packet after the presentation ends
16.explanation: Accountable next steps beat absolute claims.
